As you can read quite often on this Reddit sub, artisanal tallow CROAPs are generally all very good.


Your razor skills, your technique (and of course your skin conditions) are the most important factor. A 2 US$ Palmolive shaving cream, a 1 € Arko stick (if bought in Turkey), a 3.3 € Proraso soap (if bought in Italy) are all good enough to get great comfortable shaves.


A 14.8 US$ Stirling (5.7 oz!!) is one of the most affordable artisanal CROAPs and its mechanical properties probably reach the 93% of those of the "best" artisanal CROAPs on the market. It's a **very** good fomula.


Everyone has his/her personal preferences, almost nobody knows well the 60% or more of the most sold artisanal CROAP formulas (there are too many of them and the average shaving frequency of us seems to be every 2 or more days).


I tried more or less 7 different artisanal formulas and I would say that the products I appreciated more were made by Westman Shaving, Ariana & Evans (K2E formula), Barrister & Mann. As I said, I get great shavings by ALL the artisanal soaps I tried since they are WAY more than enough to get wonderful shavings if you already developed good skills. None of them was performing badly.


I tried just a couple of artisanal vegetal formulas (PAA CK-6 seems to me close to tallow formulas in terms of performances) and almost no hard soaps.

IMHO.

Stirling Sheep, mutton tallow. It does have a citronella citrus smell like old Dove bath soap. Purchase the refill puck option, affordable priced and just put it into your mug of choice.

Arko shaving stick soap. Tallow based, again citronella smell. Cut up the stick and mash it into your mug of choice. The cheapest priced.

Mike’s Natural Soap, shaving soap. Another tallow based. Purchase just the unscented refill puck. Pretty good price too. The only downside is it is a small artisan made and current availability might be problematic.

Other options are Mitchell’s Wool Fat shaving soap. Vegan based. Has a slight bar soap smell. If you can find affordably, currently. The company is closing. Another option is Kent Shaving Soap, refill puck. Tallow based and slightly priced shave soap. Both are from England.

Arko - cheap and smells like soap, clean and fresh. You can mold it to fit into a mug or keep it in stick-form for travel purposes. I’ve used Arko almost exclusively for years now. It’s just that good.

For cheap good quality “git r dun” soap my go-to options would be Cella (get the big brick and cut off a chunk to put in a mug), Arko (stick format but can be mashed into a mug), and Proraso. Bonus that all of these will perform better than what you were using.

Cheapest/best value: Arko. Not entirely unscented since it has what is often described as a citronella scent. But for under $5, it is the best deal in wetshaving as far as cost to performance. 

“Soap smelling” soap: Haslinger Sensitive. Relatively inexpensive, plenty slick and has a clean, soapy scent. 

Unscented: Mike’s Natural Soaps. Lots of people suggest Stirling, but to be honest I find Mike’s both slicker and easier to lather.

This would be a lot easier if you mentioned your location. Because if you're in the US, you can really do this on easy mode: just get a starter kit from Maggard Razors or Stirling.
